correctness.rationale: Under the frozen no-third-displacement hypothesis the 3n cuts are distinct. A unary relation to a named parameter selects one open one-third arc, and intersections of such short arcs are connected when nonempty. Thus the unary diagram uniquely determines a lift of one of the n projected gaps. Cut the quotient at the projection of a named vertex and consistently label its three lifts. For two coordinates in one gap, their arc/nonedge relation distinguishes the sign of the projected difference at each of the three possible lift differences; across different gaps that sign is predetermined. This makes the gap/color/order encoding bijective on finite diagrams. Any such diagram is realized by choosing small disjoint ordered projected subintervals and using density of D on each indicated lift. Homogeneity then makes the diagrams exactly the complete tuple types over the individually named base. Each fixed occupancy admits r! label assignments and within-gap orders combined, times 3^r independent colors. Stars and bars gives the claimed total, including the unique empty tuple at r=0. Uniform occupancy on these weak compositions is the Dirichlet-multinomial with all parameters one. The proof is correct for the stated pure digraph, named nonempty base and injective nonparameter tuples.
residual_risks: The finite replay is not an all-arity proof. Neither metric sampling of points nor the empty-base or unnamed-base orbit count is claimed.

evidence: Choose a₀ in A and delete it. Its forward, nonedge and backward classes are the three colors. Thus fixing a₀ is equivalent to preserving the digraph and these three colors on its complement, which by the prior bi-definability is equivalent to preserving the folded order and colors. The other n−1 named points cut that dense order into n intervals. Each interval contains all three colors densely; finite color-preserving order isomorphisms extend by back-and-forth. For a weak composition (c_i), distributing the r labels gives r!/∏c_i!, ordering them within intervals gives ∏c_i!, and colors give 3^r. The result is 3^r r! for every composition and 3^r r! binom(n+r−1,r) overall.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is an immediate application of the prior complete colored-order description and a routine labeled-order count. Equal masses, and their Dirichlet-multinomial notation, follow from that same count; they do not require any additional model-theoretic theorem.

The proof of Prop. 12 explicitly keeps the unary colors, transforms cross-color arc/nonedge relations into a linear order and identifies the result with Q₃ by rotating the two non-base sectors. It states that the order is dense and all three parts are dense.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Apply the same folding with the origin at a chosen named vertex. After that vertex is removed the sector cut has no endpoints in the remaining domain by the frozen boundary hypothesis. Rotating the sectors preserves their density, and both the digraph relations and projected order are recoverable from each other with the colors. The frozen marked-base problem is precisely the colored order orbit problem in this coordinate system.

originality.rationale: This is a direct counting corollary of the stronger structural description in Nguyen Van Thé, More on the Kechris–Pestov–Todorcevic correspondence: Precompact expansions, §8, proof of Proposition 12. That proof explicitly makes the sector-colored S(3) bi-definable with the dense three-colored linear order Q₃ by folding the three arcs. With a named vertex as the cut and that vertex removed, the same colored expansion is available: each of the three colors is exactly one of the ternary relations to the cut vertex, so the named-vertex stabilizer is precisely the automorphism group of the folded three-colored order. Any additional named vertices are just fixed labeled points of that order. Their n−1 distinct projections create n intervals. The labeled tuple orbits over those points are determined by the interval, color, and within-interval order of each new coordinate. Thus the prior structural result yields all the asserted types, not just the total, by counting colored orders in n intervals. The exact formula need not be printed in that paper to be covered.
residual_risks: An even earlier source may print the exact named-base formula; that historical question is immaterial to the demonstrated structural coverage. The differing S(3) angle in the inspected Hamann passage and the unavailable Macpherson passage are not used for the verdict.

value.rationale: The exact tuple count is natural and the exposition could be useful, but as a new finding it is mechanically implied by the known folding to Q₃. Naming one actual vertex exposes the three already known colors; fixing the other points only cuts an order into intervals. The constant mass for each occupancy is then precisely the cancellation of the labeling multinomial with within-interval factorials. The Dirichlet-multinomial restatement adds no distinct invariant or new premise. No nonroutine surviving original claim is established.
residual_risks: This verdict concerns the frozen finding as a research contribution, not the correctness or pedagogical usefulness of stating its corollary explicitly.
